standard_prerequisites.name: Commutativity on an integral scheme and additivity in the invertible sheaf
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-commutativity-on-integral (proof line 4985) and lemma-c1-cap-additive (proof line 4990)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first rewrites the cap with the Chern class of L against the divisor of f as the cap with the trivial invertible sheaf against the divisor of a meromorphic section, and the second shows that this last expression vanishes.

core_obligations: Unwind rational equivalence: for a trivial cycle alpha in Z_{k+1}(X) write it as a locally finite sum of pushforwards of principal divisors along integral closed subschemes W_j of dimension k + 2, note that the disjoint union of the W_j maps to X properly so that alpha is the pushforward of a cycle alpha' on that union, and by the projection formula transfer the problem to the union (proof lines 4959-4978).

Reduce to a single integral scheme: it suffices to show that the cap of the Chern class of the restricted invertible sheaf with each principal divisor is zero, so one may assume X integral and alpha the divisor of a rational function f (proof lines 4975-4978).

Conclude on an integral scheme: regard f as a regular meromorphic section of the structure sheaf, choose a meromorphic section s of L with divisor beta, use the commutativity statement to rewrite the cap with the Chern class of L against div(f) as the cap with the Chern class of the structure sheaf against beta, and observe that the latter vanishes by additivity (proof lines 4980-4991).
proof_roadmap: Write the trivial cycle as a sum of principal divisors and pass to the disjoint union by the projection formula (proof lines 4959-4978).
Reduce to an integral X with alpha a single principal divisor (proof lines 4975-4978).
Rewrite by commutativity on an integral scheme and conclude by additivity (proof lines 4980-4991).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the operation of capping with a first Chern class descends from cycles to the Chow group: on rationally trivial cycles it vanishes (statement lines 4947-4957, tag 02TI). The proof is a real reduction: it unfolds rational equivalence into a locally finite sum of principal divisors, uses the projection formula for the cap to reach the disjoint union of the components, reduces to a single integral scheme, and then invokes commutativity on an integral scheme together with additivity to see that the resulting expression vanishes. The two-step reduction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
